items.title: Broad breadth and positive dealer gamma, but a down tape and balanced flow withhold trend confirmation
items.note: Three surfaces disagree on conviction. Heatmap breadth is broad at 65.06% of 134 names and SPY dealers sit in positive gamma with the flip at 770.9 beneath the 775/780 wall band (spot 776.23), a backdrop that argues for a pinned, mean-reverting drift rather than a directional break. Yet the live tape is a trend day to the downside under mixed control with VWAP 776.82, and unusual options flow is now balanced (call fraction 0.5976, no longer call-led). The constructive breadth-plus-gamma structure therefore lacks tape and flow confirmation this window, so fades of extremes back toward the 775 put wall / 770.9 flip and VWAP carry more edge than strength chased into the 780 call wall.
items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth metric, the options-structure and gamma dealer regime with its flip and wall levels, the intraday session type and VWAP, and the options-flow lean, then judge whether the positive-gamma up-structure is being confirmed or contradicted by the live tape and flow.

items.title: Equity and tech risk-on drains real assets while a defensive sector leads rotation
items.note: Sector rotation is into XLC as XLE weakens and ETF momentum is led by tech (VGT 34.38%) with breadth broad, yet the real-assets book is broadly weak: silver (SLV) 14.1 and gold (GLD) 38.1 are mixed-to-soft, bitcoin (BTC-USD) 34.9 and IBIT 23.6 are in downtrends, broad commodities (DBC) 49.2 and oil (USO) 44.1 are middling uptrends, and only industrial copper (CPER 53.3) sits near the top. The divergence reads as an equity and tech risk-on advance rather than a reflation or hard-asset hedge bid, so real-asset vehicles are a poor confirmation source and a weak diversifier this window.
items.method: Compare the sector rotation into/out tickers and the ETF-momentum leader against the real-assets model scores and trends, flagging the sign divergence between equity leadership and hard-asset momentum.
